120	The eighth day, with a calmer mind. But we see
HaKadosh Baruch Hu doesn't reveal it to Moshe; He
waits through all seven days, and HaKadosh Baruch Hu knows
that Moshe thinks he is the Cohen Gadol. He lets him
make that mistake. On the eighth day,
He tells him: No, Moshe, it's not you who is the Cohen Gadol.
Go to Aharon and tell him that he is the Cohen Gadol, not
Moshe. Now let's see Aharon, who was chosen
to be the Cohen Gadol. So Moshe came to him
in the morning; he too didn't know he was to be the Cohen
Gadol. They surprised him. So Moshe came and told him: Aharon,
you have been chosen to be the Cohen Gadol.
The Midrash says that Aharon said to Moshe: I don't
know if I am suited. He had humility
and lowliness; he says: I don't know if I am suited. So
Aharon approaches the Mizbêach; he has no choice. Moshe
tells him: Listen, suited or not suited, HaKadosh
Baruch Hu says it is you. So Aharon approaches
the Mizbêach. He sees on the Mizbêach that there is fire
on the Mizbêach, the fire for offering the sacrifices. And he
sees that it is in the shape of a calf. What is this, in the shape of a calf?
After all, who made that calf, 40 days
after the giving of the Torah? Who made that calf? Aharon
made that calf. True, he did not intend to commit
idolatry, God forbid; he was forced into it. But
the Midrash says: they showed him the image of a calf on top of
the Mizbêach.
And then Aharon said to Moshe. First of all, he stopped;
he didn't want to go, out of the shame he
felt: I made a calf, and now I am about to
do this great service of offering
the sacrifices on the eighth day. So Moshe... Aharon
didn't want to go. So Moshe said to him: Why are you ashamed?
Why are you embarrassed? It is for this that you were chosen. There are
several explanations of what this means: why are you ashamed, for this you
were chosen. One explanation, said by the Or
HaChaim, by the Noam Elimelech, by the Ari HaKadosh:
What is "why are you ashamed, for this you were chosen"? Do you know
why you were chosen? Because you are ashamed. When a person is ashamed
of himself, then he can be chosen for such great
services. So he tells him: Don't be ashamed; because of this
shame, you are the one. So Aharon went
and began to offer the sacrifices. They offered all the
sacrifices, and there was a sign. HaKadosh Baruch Hu told
Moshe a sign for when the sacrifices would be accepted and I
would rest the Shechinah: when fire descends from the heavens
and consumes the sacrifices, not your fire burning
the sacrifices. On this day, such
a great day, fire must descend from heaven and burn the
sacrifices. Good. Aharon did all the services,
offered all the sacrifices.
And then they wait. Now we have to remember, everyone is waiting.
Now, the 600,000 who left Egypt is only 600,000
men from age 20 to 60; behind them, two
million people waiting to see the fire that descends from
the heavens, and Aharon stands there and waits. But fire does not
descend from heaven. It does not descend from heaven. And then
Aharon says to Moshe: Moshe, don't you see?
I told you I was not suited. Look what
shame! I offered everything. Don't you see that HaKadosh
Baruch Hu is not accepting my sacrifices? So
it is written in the Parashah that Moshe and Aharon entered into
the Ohel Moed, into the Mishkan, because Aharon asked him:
Moshe, do something, I can't bear this shame. So
Moshe and Aharon entered the Mishkan so that Moshe
would pray for Aharon not to stand in this shame. So
they entered the Mishkan and asked for mercy for Aharon,
that fire would descend from the heavens. After Moshe's prayer,
fire descended from the heavens. So up to here, fire descended from
the heavens, and there was very great joy,
a very great revelation, that HaKadosh Baruch Hu accepted
all this service. So up to here we see a little
of what Moshe and Aharon went through. It is not over
yet. Both of them, who now have to do all these
services, how do they do it? Moshe with his
shame and his pain and his jealousy that he
lost these services. Aharon with his shame:
all day he goes through corrections, this greatest day.
All day he goes through corrections. In the morning
he sees the image of a calf; then he
sees his sacrifices not being accepted; after
his sacrifices were accepted, not a few minutes passed, his two
sons Nadav and Avihu made some mistake,
with HaShem's help we will speak about it. They offered incense that they were forbidden
to offer, and both died a few minutes after
he had just had some relief,
just come out of the constriction. What do we say?
Aharon's two sons died inside the Mishkan. What
kind of day passed over Moshe and over Aharon on that day?
What shame and what pain they both went through.
The commentators ask, and Rabi Natan brings it in Likutê Halachot: Moshe and Aharon,
couldn't they have arranged a slightly better
day for them? Let's say a day that goes a little
better for them. On this day it is a must! Here we could
solve it easily: let them tell Moshe two or
three days before, "Moshe, you are not the Cohen Gadol"; he
would have prepared for it. They would not
have shown Aharon the image of an ox, the calf, on top of
the Mizbêach. But here we see a very great principle.
Here we see a very great principle: a person has to
do some service, something in spirituality,
that comes with great stature. So how will they help him
do it properly? On that very day he will have the
most unsuccessful day in the world, so he will go through
all the shames, and suddenly he will fall into jealousy and
fall into pain, and constrictions will pass over him. And why all this?
Why all this? It is truly a great innovation: so that a person
does it with inner cleanliness, without ulterior motives, without
a thought of arrogance. Moshe and Aharon, so that they would not
think: Happy is Israel that merited that we bring down
the Shechinah to them for all generations; so that there would not be...
And who needs support? Who needs help not
to stumble in arrogance? That is the real great
innovation, the great wonder. Who is it that needs the help?
Moshe and Aharon! We have no greater ones in the people of Israel
than Moshe and Aharon. Moshe Rabenu, Aharon HaCohen. Even
they need support not to stumble in the subtleties
of arrogance. Therefore it is written in the holy books:
